name: Harper Quinn
title: Porch Light
summary:
Harper Quinn is porch-light innkeeper who knows which guests are hiding. The life that shows in public is anchored at Montford Avenue inn, Asheville. Harper keeps the inn porch lit and remembers which guests actually wanted quiet. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Easygoing, wry, and good at reading a room. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: they are protecting a second person who does not know it and the person in front of them now resembles that old mistake. If that truth surfaces at Montford Avenue inn, Asheville, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
